title: The Evening Brief: Reese Breaks Two Records, Astros Change Course, Carse Waits
dek: Angel Reese set single-game and single-season WNBA rebounding records Monday as the day's sports news split between on-field milestones and off-field upheaval, from Houston's front office to a conviction in snooker and England's cricket discipline.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Angel Reese's 26-rebound game broke a 23-year-old WNBA single-game record and pushed her past A'ja Wilson for the single-season mark, the day's most concrete on-field achievement, while the Astros' sudden GM change and the Big Ten's new eligibility ban left larger institutional questions unresolved.
bottom_line: Angel Reese's 26-rebound game broke the WNBA's single-game rebounding record and pushed her past the single-season mark, the day's clearest achievement, while institutional stories moved in less settled directions: the Astros parted ways with GM Dana Brown under still-unexplained terms, the Big Ten voted to ban athletes with professional contract history from returning to college sports in direct response to a Louisiana court order, and Graeme Dott was convicted of child sexual abuse with sentencing set for 29 September. The common thread is disruption outpacing explanation, a front office reshuffled without stated cause, a conference rule built to preempt further litigation, and a cricket investigation still open around Brydon Carse. The honest read is that today's reporting documents actions and outcomes clearly but leaves several underlying reasons, the Astros' internal logic, the fuller shape of the Kanter Freedom-Natasha Cloud exchange, unestablished. Watch the August 31 injunction hearing and NFL roster cutdown, the Cricket Regulator's findings, and whether the Astros name a permanent general manager.
body: Angel Reese's night in Atlanta anchors this edition: 26 rebounds in a 78-71 win over the Los Angeles Sparks broke Chamique Holdsclaw's 23-year-old single-game WNBA record of 24, and her season total of 458 boards passed A'ja Wilson for the single-season mark. She added 11 points, three assists, three steals, and her 27th double-double of the season, capping a stretch that also included a career-high 31 points against Phoenix on Saturday.

The day's other thread is institutional disruption arriving faster than clean explanations. The Houston Astros mutually parted ways with general manager Dana Brown on August 24, with owner Jim Crane assuming interim control of baseball operations and dividing Brown's duties among assistant GMs Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey, and Connor Huff, plus senior advisor Jeff Bagwell. A separate item flagged that an MLB.com report on the same separation could not be verified in full, leaving the underlying reasoning for the move undisclosed by the club itself. The Big Ten voted unanimously to ban athletes who signed professional contracts, sat on professional rosters, or declared for the NFL Draft without withdrawing from returning to compete at member schools, a response to a Louisiana court's temporary restraining order that let players including Dae'Quan Wright return to college after NFL preseason. The SEC, ACC, Big 12, and The American are weighing similar rules, and a hearing on a full injunction is set for August 31, the same day NFL teams must cut rosters from 90 to 53.

Elsewhere, the WNBA eligibility fight from Sunday's game carried forward: Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter indefinitely banned Enes Kanter Freedom from Wintrust Arena after his ejection during the Sky-Fever game, and league sources told Front Office Sports that Kanter Freedom and Royce White are not eligible to play in the WNBA. England's cricket discipline story also continued, with pace bowler Brydon Carse still out of the squad for the second Test against Pakistan while the Cricket Regulator investigates his August 23 handcuffing outside a Derby bar; Sonny Baker has been named his replacement. Graeme Dott, snooker's 2006 world champion, was found guilty of two counts of lewd and libidinous behaviour toward a girl and boy between 1993 and 2010, with sentencing scheduled for 29 September in Edinburgh and his World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association membership permanently revoked. Separately, rugby league winger Sir Billy Boston, the first player knighted in the sport's 130-year history, died aged 92, weeks after receiving his knighthood from King Charles in 2025; he scored 571 tries in his career, a total surpassed only by Brian Bevan.

On the safety and business side, a British Medical Journal study found chronic traumatic encephalopathy in 215 of 235 deceased NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 and donated their brains to research, establishing a conservative minimum prevalence of 24.5% and a maximum of 97.7%. The PGA Tour announced the Tour Championship will shift to a two-week, match-play format in 2028, ending East Lake's run as permanent host since 2004. Kalshi signed partnerships with the Braves, Red Sox, Dodgers, Padres, and Giants, bringing prediction-market deals to seven MLB teams. Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase walked off practice after a knee hyperextension he described as minor, and Portland's Shaedon Sharpe tore his meniscus in an offseason workout and is expected out six months. ESPN announced RedZone will cover the US Open starting August 30, its first sport beyond football, and Karl Ravech called his final ESPN broadcast after 33 years, a Little League Classic game he covered following his July layoff.

Why these things happened varies by story. The Astros' front-office change is described only as mutual, with Front Office Sports noting Crane previously ran a similar interim stretch after firing James Click in 2022; the deeper motivation is not established in the reporting. The Big Ten's ban is a direct response to the Louisiana court order and the precedent it set for players like Wright. The WNBA ban followed directly from Sunday's ejection and the league's existing CBA language restricting play to women, though the league's broader policy on Kanter Freedom's arena access elsewhere is not yet clear. Carse's removal remains precautionary pending the Cricket Regulator's investigation, not a stated finding of wrongdoing.
Desk boards were unavailable for this edition, so all figures above come from the day's published reporting rather than a live scoreboard.

The coming days carry several checkpoints: the Cricket Regulator's investigation into Carse and any resulting charges, Dott's 29 September sentencing, the August 31 hearing on a full injunction in the Louisiana eligibility case alongside the NFL's roster cutdown to 53 that could produce new eligibility claimants, confirmation of whether the Astros name a permanent general manager, medical updates on Chase and Sharpe, and whether other Power Four conferences formally adopt bans matching the Big Ten's.
